summary: Walnut sits in the eastern San Gabriel Valley on a landscape of rolling hills and shallow canyons that would surprise anyone who pictures the Inland Empire as flat sprawl — the terrain rises and dips enough that many streets offer long western sightlines toward the San Gabriel Mountains, and the city's nine square miles encompass genuine elevation change rather than gridded plains. With a median household income of nearly $134,000 and a median home price of $972,500, the price-to-income ratio hovers around 7.3×, meaning purchasing requires substantial down payments or dual high earners even at the local median — yet rents at $3,120 consume a more manageable ~28% of that same income. The city functions largely as a bedroom community: Mt. San Antonio College is the most prominent local institution, but most professional employment pulls commuters west toward downtown Los Angeles or south toward the Orange County job corridors along the 57 and 60 freeways, which bracket the city. Evening life is quiet-suburban rather than walkable-downtown; retail clusters along Lemon Avenue and Grand Avenue but there is no traditional Main Street grid. Annual sunshine averaging 9.3 hours a day and nighttime lows rarely dipping below the mid-50s make the hilly terrain genuinely usable year-round for walking. Walnut is a place where the geography promises more character than the built environment delivers — lush hills and canyon views wrapped in a commuter-oriented street network.
